_doc: The numbers mcgyvr DERIVES on a rig by measurement, stated as data rather than as literals in code. Filed 2026-09-12 to close the gap the per-rig-numbers task named: several rig- or engine-specific measured values were hard-coded in `src/`, so the number lived where the measurement's provenance could not, and nothing would notice it drifting from the rig it described. A value here is the single source of truth; code that sizes a rig or locks a fleet looks it up, and an absent value is a named refusal, never a silent inline default. `tools/runs/hosts.json` is the sibling declaration of what each rig IS (read live by gate 2); this file states what was MEASURED on it. It is JSON and content-addressable so a reader can digest it the way it digests `hosts.json`.
_numbers_doc: Per-host `numbers` blocks: a value derived from measurement on that rig, carried nowhere else in code. The key is read by `src/mcgyvr/derived.py`; a rig or value that is absent is refused by name.

runtime_resident_gb.why: Host RAM beyond the spilled experts themselves (context, compute buffers, copy paths). Swept across six --n-cpu-moe cells on srv2 (records/measurements/serving-sweep-2026-08-25/): RSS - offloaded expert bytes sat flat at 1.52-1.53 GiB at every setting from 4 to 20 blocks, which is what makes it an intercept rather than a rate. Declared at the same 1.53 for srv1, which has no separate sweep; a differing srv1 reading would replace this value, not the lookup.

card_remainder_mib.why: The unnamed remainder of the card's non-expert constant `C` after every named term is accounted for, net of the card's idle baseline, on srv1 (src/mcgyvr/serving/vramfit.py's derivation of C; records/measurements/measuring-gaps-2026-09-10/ Q4/Q6, records/measurements/flexibility-2026-09-09/ Q11). It is recorded here because it is per-rig; `C` itself is per (model, serve config) and subsumes it.

It is recorded here because it is per-rig; `C` itself is per (model, serve config) and subsumes it.

engine._doc: Engine-specific measured numbers, shared across rigs. Keyed by engine rather than by host because the figure belongs to the backend, not to the machine it runs on.

warm_decode_class_pct._doc: The percent a unit's warm decode may fall, by the unit's tolerance class (`mcgyvr.fleet.tolerance.tolerance_class`: engine vllm is `vllm`; llama.cpp with experts on the CPU is `cpu_experts`; any other llama.cpp is `llamacpp`): what the fleet lock allows it to lose to NVMe against its no-NVMe baseline, and what a live probe judges its warm decode against. It does not cover prefill, which has its own measured classes in `prefill_class_pct` (owner, 2026-09-15). Owner, 2026-09-15: the measured classes replace the survey's provisional per-engine `warm_decode_pct` (vllm 3.0, llama.cpp 5.0).

vllm.why: The measured class tolerance, records/measurements/fleet-identity-2026-09-11/tolerances.json classes.vllm.tolerance_pct (worst shortfall 0.58% over 15 samples per arm on srv2's 3B and 7B, M1 rule in records/plans/fleet-identity-measurements-2026-09-11.md).

llamacpp.why: The measured class tolerance, records/measurements/fleet-identity-2026-09-11/tolerances.json classes.llamacpp.tolerance_pct (worst shortfall 0.52% over 15 samples per arm on srv1's Ling-3.0-tiny, M1 rule in records/plans/fleet-identity-measurements-2026-09-11.md).

cpu_experts.why: The measured class tolerance, records/measurements/fleet-identity-2026-09-11/tolerances.json classes.cpu_experts.tolerance_pct (worst shortfall 47.84% over 15 samples on srv1's Qwen3.6-35B-A3B with experts on the CPU, M1 rule in records/plans/fleet-identity-measurements-2026-09-11.md).

prefill_class_pct._doc: The percent a unit's prefill may fall below its locked as-run value when a live probe judges it, by the same tolerance class as `warm_decode_class_pct` (`mcgyvr.fleet.tolerance.tolerance_class`). Owner, 2026-09-15: prefill is judged by its own measured class tolerances, not by warm decode's. Measured with NVMe offload disabled by M1's rule in records/measurements/fleet-identity-prefill-2026-09-12/README.md; vLLM's value is records/plans/fleet-identity.md §12 'Prefill tolerance — ruled 8%' (B89).

vllm.why: The ruled vLLM prefill tolerance (records/plans/fleet-identity.md §12, B89): the worst single-sample shortfall after dropping the single restart-tail outlier, rounded up. That is srv2's 3B, records/measurements/fleet-identity-prefill-2026-09-12/results-prefill.json per_unit shortfall_pct 7.86 over 15 samples. The rule's raw classes.vllm.tolerance_pct 22 rests on one 7B sample of 9,460 tok/s, the tail of a restart, which the ruling drops (README.md there).

llamacpp.why: The measured class tolerance, records/measurements/fleet-identity-prefill-2026-09-12/results-prefill.json classes.llamacpp.tolerance_pct (worst shortfall 0.37% over 15 samples on srv1's Ling-3.0-tiny, floored to the rule's 1%).

cpu_experts.why: The measured class tolerance, records/measurements/fleet-identity-prefill-2026-09-12/results-prefill.json classes.cpu_experts.tolerance_pct (worst shortfall 0.13% over 15 samples on srv1's Qwen3.6-35B-A3B with --n-cpu-moe 30, floored to the rule's 1%).

_procedure_doc: Read by `src/mcgyvr/derived.py` (`class_tolerances`, keyed by judged field). `runtime_resident_gb` is consumed by `src/mcgyvr/serving/__init__.py` (`_host_gb`) when an MoE spills experts to host RAM; `warm_decode_class_pct` is consumed by `src/mcgyvr/cli.py` (`_fleet_lock`, passed to `mcgyvr.fleet.lock.write`) and by `mcgyvr.fleet.probe`; `prefill_class_pct` is consumed by `mcgyvr.fleet.probe`. `card_remainder_mib` is provenance for `src/mcgyvr/serving/vramfit.py` and is not consumed by any code path.
